changes.before: This Praxis establishes an empirical design basis for cascaded uniform resource locator (URL) phishing detection through CyberSentinel, a system combining structural classification, a character transformer and distribution monitoring. Three research questions connect representation, monitoring and selective execution to detection quality and service cost. Paired cross-dataset comparisons, controlled input interventions and service measurements explain how these design choices affect system behavior. Structural features increase internal recall by 64.07 percentage points. Validation controls reveal a strong association between URL format and class labels, while fixed-weight interventions establish sensitivity to scheme spelling. Together, these findings identify representation dependence without assigning an unmeasured share of the internal gain to format. Paired model outputs establish a 90.5487% false-positive floor for routing between unchanged decisions on the evaluated external cohort, making the expert’s available corrections a measurable design constraint. Monitoring detects 87.12% of external windows, while escalation adds 218 false positives without additional gold-positive detections, demonstrating the importance of evaluating alerts through their resulting decisions. Controlled service experiments identify an effective implementation change: worker-owned clients reduce median paired 95th-percentile latency by 79.68% in single-host synthetic structural-only measurements, with a no-model control supporting the client-path explanation. The resulting contribution is concrete engineering guidance: evaluate representation stability alongside detection, select experts for useful corrections, measure monitoring through response outcomes, and target execution costs identified by controlled measurement.
changes.after: This Praxis builds and tests CyberSentinel, a uniform resource locator (URL) phishing gateway combining structural classification, a character transformer, distribution monitoring and a Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) service. Internal structural recall reaches 98.6807% at a 0.7747% false-positive rate, a 64.07-percentage-point gain over length alone. Controlled experiments explain the system's behavior and test improvements. Validation labels are strongly associated with URL format, and scheme spelling changes frozen-model decisions; these tests do not quantify the format's share of the internal gain. On the evaluated external cohort, shared errors impose an exact 90.5487% false-positive floor on routing between unchanged decisions. Monitoring recognizes 87.12% of external windows, exceeding its sensitivity target, while audit false alerts exceed their limit. Escalation adds 218 false positives without another gold detection, establishing the need to evaluate alerts and subsequent decisions separately. In single-host synthetic structural-only service tests, worker-owned clients reduce median paired 95th-percentile latency by 79.68%, preserving every comparable prediction. A no-model control supports the client-path explanation. The complete gateway did not meet its prespecified joint hypotheses; the experiments identify the governing constraints and test concrete remedies. CyberSentinel contributes a working architecture, a measured service improvement, a benchmark-format check and an exact bound that guides expert selection.

changes.before: An inline phishing gateway must detect threats, limit false warnings and respond promptly. The design challenge is to make those requirements work together: expert calls consume resources, and recall gains must justify their false-alert cost. This study evaluates a low-cost structural detector, selective character-model execution and distribution monitoring against joint detection and service constraints. That joint evaluation gives each component's contribution an operational meaning.
changes.after: An inline phishing gateway must detect threats, limit false warnings and respond promptly. A cheap first model saves computation; an expert may recognize patterns it misses. A distribution monitor flags inputs that differ from the training reference. CyberSentinel tests these components together under joint detection and service constraints. Each must earn its place through better decisions or lower cost.
